title: Python authenticated fragmentation uses broadcast instead of exact peer target
description: Node._transmit_peer_schc and reassembly response paths call LinkLayer.send(fragment/control) with default AddrMode.NONE and empty destination; _AuthenticatedReassemblyManager._local_target accepts that broadcast as local. Every node that pins the signer and has a compatible policy can allocate/mutate a distinct (its_local, signer, rule) session and emit broadcast ACK/abort, defeating exact hop-by-hop endpoint binding and diverging from Rust's Extended-unicast control requirement. Send fragments and controls to the peer's authenticated IID with AddrMode.EXTENDED and reject NONE/SHORT for authenticated fragmentation. Add overhearing/multi-node/wrong-target/response-target tests.
notes: Robustness acceptance: ACK/abort responses must also use Priority.ACK and the bounded control deadline rather than default BULK/120s, while data fragments retain the intended data priority.
